<section id="A5" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix E </span>Training details</h2>

<section id="A5.SS0.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Tile size.</h4>

<div id="A5.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A5.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">All experiments are pre-trained on <math id="A5.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="64\times 64" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>64</mn><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mn>64</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">64\times 64</annotation></semantics></math> tiles sampled from all
six cubed-sphere faces. The production STRATA model is further fine-tuned on
<math id="A5.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="128\times 128" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>128</mn><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mn>128</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">128\times 128</annotation></semantics></math> tiles (see below).</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A5.SS0.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Normalization.</h4>

<div id="A5.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A5.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Each input and output channel is normalized independently
by subtracting its global mean and dividing by its global standard deviation,
computed over subsampled training data.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A5.SS0.SSS0.Px3" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Optimization.</h4>

<div id="A5.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A5.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We use AdamW with <math id="A5.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\beta_{1}=0.9" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>β</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>0.9</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\beta_{1}=0.9</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="A5.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\beta_{2}=0.999" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>β</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>0.999</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\beta_{2}=0.999</annotation></semantics></math>, weight decay <math id="A5.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="10^{-5}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">10^{-5}</annotation></semantics></math>,
and Smoothed <math id="A5.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\ell_{1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\ell_{1}</annotation></semantics></math> loss (Huber loss with <math id="A5.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\delta=1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>δ</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\delta=1</annotation></semantics></math>).
Training uses a total batch size of 8 or 16
(1 sample per GPU across 8 or 16 H100 80 GB GPUs)
with BF16 mixed precision and <span id="A5.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">torch.compile</span>.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A5.SS0.SSS0.Px4" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Learning rate.</h4>

<div id="A5.SS0.SSS0.Px4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A5.SS0.SSS0.Px4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The isoFLOP sweep (Figure <a href="#S3.F3" title="Figure 3 ‣ 3.2 Architecture ‣ 3 Proposed Method ‣ Scaling Storm-Resolving Atmospheric AI Simulation to the Entire Planet" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3</span></a>, Table <a href="#A2.T2" title="Table S2 ‣ B.2 Patch-Size and Model-Size Sweep ‣ Appendix B Architecture details ‣ Scaling Storm-Resolving Atmospheric AI Simulation to the Entire Planet" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">S2</span></a>)
uses a constant lr <math id="A5.SS0.SSS0.Px4.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="=10^{-4}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>=</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">=10^{-4}</annotation></semantics></math> on 8 H100 GPUs; three configurations
(DiT-S-ps4, DiT-M-ps4, DiT-L-ps2) receive an additional dampened cosine
fine-tuning stage with 2 cycles.
PixelDiT-S (DiT-S backbone with standard PixelDiT decoder) and
PixelDiT-M (DiT-M backbone) both use dampened cosine LR
(initial <math id="A5.SS0.SSS0.Px4.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="5\times 10^{-4}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>5</mn><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">5\times 10^{-4}</annotation></semantics></math>, decay factor <math id="A5.SS0.SSS0.Px4.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.3162" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.3162</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.3162</annotation></semantics></math>): PixelDiT-S trains for
2 cycles and 32 M samples; PixelDiT-M for 3 cycles and 18 M samples.
The production STRATA model shares the pretrained PixelDiT-M architecture weights but
replaces linear-projection upsampling with bilinear/convolutional upsampling
(Figure <a href="#A2.F1" title="Figure S1 ‣ B.1 STRATA Architecture and Production Hyperparameters ‣ Appendix B Architecture details ‣ Scaling Storm-Resolving Atmospheric AI Simulation to the Entire Planet" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">S1</span></a>) and is trained in three stages:
(1) pixel block warm-up with DiT layers frozen, cosine decay from
<math id="A5.SS0.SSS0.Px4.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="5\times 10^{-4}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>5</mn><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">5\times 10^{-4}</annotation></semantics></math>, 1 cycle, 6 M samples;
(2) joint fine-tuning of all layers, cosine decay from <math id="A5.SS0.SSS0.Px4.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="5\times 10^{-4}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>5</mn><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">5\times 10^{-4}</annotation></semantics></math>
with decay factor <math id="A5.SS0.SSS0.Px4.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.3162" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.3162</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.3162</annotation></semantics></math>, 2 cycles, 12 M samples;
(3) large-tile fine-tuning on <math id="A5.SS0.SSS0.Px4.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="128\times 128" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>128</mn><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mn>128</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">128\times 128</annotation></semantics></math> tiles,
constant lr <math id="A5.SS0.SSS0.Px4.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="=10^{-5}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>=</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">=10^{-5}</annotation></semantics></math>, 1.5 M samples.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A5.SS0.SSS0.Px5" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Multi-step fine-tuning.</h4>

<div id="A5.SS0.SSS0.Px5.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A5.SS0.SSS0.Px5.p1.1" class="ltx_p">After convergence of the one-step model,
we fine-tune autoregressively to improve multi-step rollout stability.
For an <math id="A5.SS0.SSS0.Px5.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>N</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N</annotation></semantics></math>-step fine-tuning pass,
the model is rolled out for <math id="A5.SS0.SSS0.Px5.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N-1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N-1</annotation></semantics></math> steps under <span id="A5.SS0.SSS0.Px5.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">torch.no_grad()</span>
and a Smoothed <math id="A5.SS0.SSS0.Px5.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\ell_{1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\ell_{1}</annotation></semantics></math> loss is computed only on the final prediction;
forcing fields are provided at every rollout step.
We first fine-tune for 2,000 gradient steps with <math id="A5.SS0.SSS0.Px5.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N=2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N=2</annotation></semantics></math>,
then for a further 2,000 steps with <math id="A5.SS0.SSS0.Px5.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N=4" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N=4</annotation></semantics></math>,
both at a constant learning rate of <math id="A5.SS0.SSS0.Px5.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="10^{-5}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">10^{-5}</annotation></semantics></math>.
Multi-step fine-tuning suppresses ripple-style artifacts
that accumulate in one-step-trained rollouts.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="A6" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix F </span>Inference</h2>

<section id="A6.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">F.1 </span>Tile extraction and DUO-style boundary padding</h3>

<div id="A6.SS1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A6.SS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">SCREAM’s cubed-sphere grid is defined by equiangular meshes
on each cube face.
To construct halo cells beyond a face boundary,
we extend the face’s equiangular mesh on its own plane
past the boundary—preserving the same angular spacing
as the interior—and then project these extended planar coordinates
back onto the sphere.
The state values at these extended grid points are interpolated
from the 4 nearest neighbors on the adjacent face,
weighted by inverse distance.
The resulting halo is a seamless continuation
of the face’s own grid pattern.</p>
</div>
<section id="A6.SS1.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Tile stitching</h4>

<div id="A6.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A6.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Tiles are extracted with a stride smaller than the tile size
so that adjacent tiles share a border region.
Each tile’s output is weighted by a 2D Kaiser–Bessel-derived window,
which tapers smoothly to zero at the edges;
the final value at each grid cell is the weighted average
of all overlapping tile outputs.
This blending eliminates tile-boundary discontinuities
in the stitched global state.
If the output window function is instead chosen to be a 2D top-hat filter that is 1 in the interior and 0 in the halo region, then the stitching operation reduces to simply a crop.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A6.SS1.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Linear operator interpretation</h4>

<div id="A6.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A6.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">For implementation, it is helpful to express padding and stitching as sparse linear operators <math id="A6.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="P" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>P</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">P</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A6.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>S</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S</annotation></semantics></math>, respectively.
Let <math id="A6.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{x}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>𝐱</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{x}</annotation></semantics></math> be the un-padded input and <math id="A6.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{y}=P\mathbf{x}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>𝐲</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>P</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>𝐱</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{y}=P\mathbf{x}</annotation></semantics></math> be the padded output.
Concretely, the rows of <math id="A6.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="P" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>P</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">P</annotation></semantics></math> expressed in matrix form have 4 non-zero elements corresponding to the weights of the 4 nearest neighbors.
The stitching <math id="A6.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>S</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S</annotation></semantics></math> is an approximate inverse of <math id="A6.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="P" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>P</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">P</annotation></semantics></math> expressed as</p>
<table id="A6.E5" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A6.E5.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S=D^{-1}P^{T}W" display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>S</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><msup><mi>D</mi><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>P</mi><mi>T</mi></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>W</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S=D^{-1}P^{T}W</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(5)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A6.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.2" class="ltx_p">where <math id="A6.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="W" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>W</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">W</annotation></semantics></math> is diagonal matrix consisting of the weights of the window and <math id="A6.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="D=P^{T}W\mathbf{1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>D</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><msup><mi>P</mi><mi>T</mi></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>W</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mn>𝟏</mn></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">D=P^{T}W\mathbf{1}</annotation></semantics></math> is the sum of the incoming weights; <math id="A6.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{1}=[1,\ldots,1]^{T}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>𝟏</mn><mo>=</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><mi>T</mi></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{1}=[1,\ldots,1]^{T}</annotation></semantics></math>.
Interpreted in terms of message passing, <math id="A6.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="P" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>P</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">P</annotation></semantics></math> sends a unique message from each unpadded grid point and <math id="A6.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>S</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S</annotation></semantics></math> takes a weighted average of the return communications.</p>
</div>
<div id="A6.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A6.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Eq. <a href="#A6.E5" title="In Linear operator interpretation ‣ F.1 Tile extraction and DUO-style boundary padding ‣ Appendix F Inference ‣ Scaling Storm-Resolving Atmospheric AI Simulation to the Entire Planet" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5</span></a> is helpful for implementing the stitching operation because <math id="A6.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="P^{T}(W\mathbf{y})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>P</mi><mi>T</mi></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>W</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>𝐲</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">P^{T}(W\mathbf{y})</annotation></semantics></math> is just the vector-Jacobian product of the forward operator <math id="A6.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="P" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>P</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">P</annotation></semantics></math> applied on a <math id="A6.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="W\mathbf{y}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>W</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>𝐲</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">W\mathbf{y}</annotation></semantics></math>, and can in principle be computed using the automatic differentiation feature of modern deep learning frameworks.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A6.SS1.SSS0.Px3" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Distributed Implementation</h4>

<div id="A6.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A6.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The tile based inference approach also enables scalability to a distributed environment. Each rank processes a subset of tiles and model compute is independent across tiles. However, the DUO-style boundary padding outlined above needs to be consistent across processes.
We can do this by performing a communication so every process has all the data needed for the DUO-style halo cell computation to populate the halos for all local tiles.
This communication needs to be performed once per time-step to keep tiles in sync and ensure seamless continuation of fields across tile boundaries.
In a simple implementation, the padding operator <math id="A6.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="P\mathbf{x}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>P</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>𝐱</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">P\mathbf{x}</annotation></semantics></math> can be applied using an all-gather followed by interpolation to the process-owned tiles using a sliced version of <math id="A6.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="P" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>P</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">P</annotation></semantics></math>.
In block matrix form, this is given by</p>
<table id="A6.E6" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A6.E6.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="P=diag([P_{1},\ldots,P_{n}])G," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>P</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>i</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>a</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>g</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><msub><mi>P</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>P</mi><mi>n</mi></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>G</mi></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">P=diag([P_{1},\ldots,P_{n}])G,</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(6)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A6.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p1.2" class="ltx_p">where <math id="A6.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="P_{j}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>P</mi><mi>j</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">P_{j}</annotation></semantics></math> is the slice of <math id="A6.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="P" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>P</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">P</annotation></semantics></math> owned by process <math id="A6.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="j" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>j</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">j</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A6.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="G" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>G</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">G</annotation></semantics></math> is an all-gather.
This is simple, but most of the data communicated is unused, so it is more efficient to communicate only the tile boundary data needed for the 4 nearest neighbor interpolation. This reduces the all-gather to a local peer-to-peer communication pattern leveraging locality of the halo cell neighbor interpolation.</p>
</div>
<div id="A6.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A6.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p2.1" class="ltx_p">To implement the stitching operator <math id="A6.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>S</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S</annotation></semantics></math>, the all-gather framing is helpful in light of Eq. <a href="#A6.E5" title="In Linear operator interpretation ‣ F.1 Tile extraction and DUO-style boundary padding ‣ Appendix F Inference ‣ Scaling Storm-Resolving Atmospheric AI Simulation to the Entire Planet" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5</span></a>.
The only expression in that equation requiring communication is <math id="A6.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="P^{T}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>P</mi><mi>T</mi></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">P^{T}</annotation></semantics></math>.
In this form,</p>
<table id="A6.Ex2" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A6.Ex2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="P^{T}=G^{T}diag([P_{1}^{T},\ldots,P_{n}^{T}])" display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>P</mi><mi>T</mi></msup><mo>=</mo><mrow><msup><mi>G</mi><mi>T</mi></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>d</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>i</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>a</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>g</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><msubsup><mi>P</mi><mn>1</mn><mi>T</mi></msubsup><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><msubsup><mi>P</mi><mi>n</mi><mi>T</mi></msubsup></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">P^{T}=G^{T}diag([P_{1}^{T},\ldots,P_{n}^{T}])</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A6.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p2.2" class="ltx_p">Since the second part of this expression is block-diagonal it can be applied locally on each process independently. Then, the transpose of the all-gather <math id="A6.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="G^{T}\mathbf{v}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>G</mi><mi>T</mi></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>𝐯</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">G^{T}\mathbf{v}</annotation></semantics></math> can be implemented as a distributed reduce-scatter operation.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A6.SS1.SSS0.Px4" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Scaling</h4>

<div id="A6.SS1.SSS0.Px4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A6.SS1.SSS0.Px4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Figure <a href="#A6.F5" title="Figure S5 ‣ Scaling ‣ F.1 Tile extraction and DUO-style boundary padding ‣ Appendix F Inference ‣ Scaling Storm-Resolving Atmospheric AI Simulation to the Entire Planet" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">S5</span></a> shows the scalability of this distributed inference through a strong scaling test from 8 to 512 GPUs using a 2D top-hat window function. Both the all-gather and neighbor peer-to-peer algorithms have very good scalability with the all-gather algorithm yielding 82.8% strong scaling efficiency at 512 GPUs and the neighbor peer-to-peer algorithm yields 98.4% efficiency at the same scale.</p>
</div>
<figure id="A6.F5" class="ltx_figure"><object type="image/svg+xml" data="2606.31248v1/scaling.svg" id="A6.F5.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:452/189;" width="452" height="189"></object>
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure">Figure S5: </span><span id="A6.F5.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Scalability of tile based distributed inference.</span>
Left: Per step wall-clock time. Right: Speedup over 8 GPU baseline in solid lines on the left y-axis and strong scaling efficiency in dashed lines on the right y-axis. Two DUO-style boundary padding implementations are shown: allgather (blue) and neighbor peer-to-peer (orange).</figcaption>
</figure>
</section>
</section>
<section id="A6.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">F.2 </span>Spectral filter to control large-scale vertical velocity</h3>

<div id="A6.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A6.SS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Tile-based training is blind to global-mean constraints:
because tiles are processed independently,
the model has no mechanism to enforce that the global-mean vertical
pressure velocity <math id="A6.SS2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\omega" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>ω</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\omega</annotation></semantics></math> remains near zero (as required by mass continuity),
causing a slow drift in the leading spherical harmonic modes of <math id="A6.SS2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\omega" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>ω</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\omega</annotation></semantics></math>
over long rollouts.
After each rollout step we remove the drift by computing the real
spherical harmonic transform of <math id="A6.SS2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\omega" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>ω</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\omega</annotation></semantics></math> at each vertical level,
zeroing out the leading three modes (<math id="A6.SS2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\ell=0,1,2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\ell=0,1,2</annotation></semantics></math>),
and inverting the transform.</p>
</div>
<figure id="A6.F6" class="ltx_figure"><object type="image/svg+xml" data="2606.31248v1/paper_precip_timeseries_omegafilter_compare_n144_s6.svg" id="A6.F6.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:238/162;" width="238" height="162"></object>
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure">Figure S6: </span><span id="A6.F6.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Effect of the large-scale <math id="A6.F6.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\omega" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>ω</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\omega</annotation></semantics></math> filter on global-mean precipitation.</span>
Global-mean liquid precipitation rate over a 24-hour rollout for
SCREAM (reference, solid blue), STRATA with the <math id="A6.F6.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\omega" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>ω</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\omega</annotation></semantics></math> filter
(dashed orange), and STRATA without the filter (dotted green).
Without the filter, unconstrained drift in the leading spherical-harmonic
modes of <math id="A6.F6.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\omega" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>ω</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\omega</annotation></semantics></math> causes global-mean precipitation to collapse to
<math id="A6.F6.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{\sim}1.0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>∼</mo><mn>1.0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{\sim}1.0</annotation></semantics></math> mm d<sup id="A6.F6.5" class="ltx_sup"><span id="A6.F6.5.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">-1</span></sup> by 24 h—roughly half the reference value.
The filter substantially reduces this dry drift while leaving the
fine-scale precipitation structure unchanged.</figcaption>
</figure>
</section>
<section id="A6.SS3" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">F.3 </span>Negative <math id="A6.SS3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="q_{v}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>q</mi><mi>v</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">q_{v}</annotation></semantics></math> and precipitation fixer.</h3>

<div id="A6.SS3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A6.SS3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Without explicit constraints the model can predict physically inadmissible
negative specific humidity <math id="A6.SS3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="q_{v}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>q</mi><mi>v</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">q_{v}</annotation></semantics></math> or precipitation.
We apply differentiable constraints in the forward pass,
active during both fine-tuning and rollout,
so the model learns outputs consistent with the constraints.
For <math id="A6.SS3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="q_{v}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>q</mi><mi>v</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">q_{v}</annotation></semantics></math>, let <math id="A6.SS3.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r=\Delta q_{v}/\max(q_{v}^{t},\,\varepsilon)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>q</mi><mi>v</mi></msub></mrow><mo>/</mo><mrow><mi>max</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msubsup><mi>q</mi><mi>v</mi><mi>t</mi></msubsup><mo rspace="0.337em">,</mo><mi>ε</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r=\Delta q_{v}/\max(q_{v}^{t},\,\varepsilon)</annotation></semantics></math>
with <math id="A6.SS3.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\varepsilon=10^{-14}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>ε</mi><mo>=</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>14</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\varepsilon=10^{-14}</annotation></semantics></math> kg kg<sup id="A6.SS3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_sup"><span id="A6.SS3.p1.1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">-1</span></sup>.
We constrain <math id="A6.SS3.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>r</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r</annotation></semantics></math> via <math id="A6.SS3.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tilde{r}=\mathrm{softplus}(r+1;\,\beta=10)-1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>r</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>softplus</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mi>β</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>10</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tilde{r}=\mathrm{softplus}(r+1;\,\beta=10)-1</annotation></semantics></math>
and set <math id="A6.SS3.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="q_{v}^{t+1}=(1+\tilde{r})\,\max(q_{v}^{t},\,\varepsilon)\geq 0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi>q</mi><mi>v</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msubsup><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><mover accent="true"><mi>r</mi><mo>~</mo></mover></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0.337em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mi>max</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msubsup><mi>q</mi><mi>v</mi><mi>t</mi></msubsup><mo rspace="0.337em">,</mo><mi>ε</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>≥</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">q_{v}^{t+1}=(1+\tilde{r})\,\max(q_{v}^{t},\,\varepsilon)\geq 0</annotation></semantics></math>.
During rollout only, an additional hard floor of <math id="A6.SS3.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="10^{-15}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>15</mn></mrow></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">10^{-15}</annotation></semantics></math> kg kg<sup id="A6.SS3.p1.1.2" class="ltx_sup"><span id="A6.SS3.p1.1.2.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">-1</span></sup>
eliminates any residual numerical negatives.
For surface precipitation, the predicted value is denormalized,
passed through ReLU, and renormalized.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="A7" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix G </span>Throughput and Energy Accounting</h2>

<div id="A7.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A7.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We report inference throughput in simulated days per wall-clock day (SDPD) and
energy efficiency in simulated days per megawatt-hour
(<math id="A7.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{SD\,MWh^{-1}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>SD</mi><mo lspace="0.170em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>MWh</mi><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{SD\,MWh^{-1}}</annotation></semantics></math>). For STRATA, one simulated day contains
<math id="A7.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N_{\mathrm{step}}=24\,\mathrm{h}/10\,\mathrm{min}=144" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>N</mi><mi>step</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mrow><mn>24</mn><mo lspace="0.170em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>h</mi></mrow><mo>/</mo><mn>10</mn></mrow><mo lspace="0.170em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>min</mi></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>144</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N_{\mathrm{step}}=24\,\mathrm{h}/10\,\mathrm{min}=144</annotation></semantics></math> autoregressive steps.
If <math id="A7.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t_{\mathrm{step}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>t</mi><mi>step</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t_{\mathrm{step}}</annotation></semantics></math> is the measured wall-clock latency of one global
autoregressive step, then</p>
<table id="A7.E7" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A7.E7.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{SDPD}=\frac{86400}{N_{\mathrm{step}}t_{\mathrm{step}}}." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>SDPD</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>86400</mn><mrow><msub><mi>N</mi><mi>step</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>t</mi><mi>step</mi></msub></mrow></mfrac></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{SDPD}=\frac{86400}{N_{\mathrm{step}}t_{\mathrm{step}}}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(7)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A7.p1.2" class="ltx_p">Given an average power draw <math id="A7.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="P" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>P</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">P</annotation></semantics></math> in MW for the hardware included in the
accounting boundary, the corresponding energy-normalized throughput is</p>
<table id="A7.E8" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A7.E8.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{SD\,MWh^{-1}}=\frac{\mathrm{SDPD}}{24P}." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>SD</mi><mo lspace="0.170em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>MWh</mi><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mi>SDPD</mi><mrow><mn>24</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>P</mi></mrow></mfrac></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{SD\,MWh^{-1}}=\frac{\mathrm{SDPD}}{24P}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(8)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A7.p1.3" class="ltx_p">Equivalently, if <math id="A7.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t_{\mathrm{SD}}=N_{\mathrm{step}}t_{\mathrm{step}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>t</mi><mi>SD</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>N</mi><mi>step</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>t</mi><mi>step</mi></msub></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t_{\mathrm{SD}}=N_{\mathrm{step}}t_{\mathrm{step}}</annotation></semantics></math> is the
wall-clock seconds required for one simulated day, then
<math id="A7.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{SD\,MWh^{-1}}=1/(Pt_{\mathrm{SD}}/3600)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>SD</mi><mo lspace="0.170em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>MWh</mi><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>P</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>t</mi><mi>SD</mi></msub></mrow><mo>/</mo><mn>3600</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{SD\,MWh^{-1}}=1/(Pt_{\mathrm{SD}}/3600)</annotation></semantics></math>.
For SCREAM, we use the same conversion from its reported SDPD and average
system power, and compute speedups as the ratio of
<math id="A7.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{SD\,MWh^{-1}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>SD</mi><mo lspace="0.170em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>MWh</mi><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{SD\,MWh^{-1}}</annotation></semantics></math> between STRATA and SCREAM. Under the assumptions
in Table <a href="#A7.T5" title="Table S5 ‣ Appendix G Throughput and Energy Accounting ‣ Scaling Storm-Resolving Atmospheric AI Simulation to the Entire Planet" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">S5</span></a>, the production STRATA configuration achieves
<math id="A7.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="48.1\,\mathrm{SD\,MWh^{-1}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>48.1</mn><mo lspace="0.170em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>SD</mi><mo lspace="0.170em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>MWh</mi><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">48.1\,\mathrm{SD\,MWh^{-1}}</annotation></semantics></math>, a <math id="A7.p1.m9" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="{&gt;}50\times" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>50</mn><mo lspace="0.222em">×</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{&gt;}50\times</annotation></semantics></math> energy-efficiency
improvement over the SCREAM Frontier run
(<math id="A7.p1.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.78\,\mathrm{SD\,MWh^{-1}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>0.78</mn><mo lspace="0.170em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>SD</mi><mo lspace="0.170em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>MWh</mi><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.78\,\mathrm{SD\,MWh^{-1}}</annotation></semantics></math>).
Using an emissions factor of <math id="A7.p1.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="388\,\mathrm{kg\,CO_{2}\,MWh^{-1}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>388</mn><mo lspace="0.170em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>kg</mi><mo lspace="0.170em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>CO</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>MWh</mi><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">388\,\mathrm{kg\,CO_{2}\,MWh^{-1}}</annotation></semantics></math> (<a href="https://www.eia.gov/tools/faqs/faq.php?id=74&amp;t=11" title="" class="ltx_ref ltx_url ltx_font_typewriter">https://www.eia.gov/tools/faqs/faq.php?id=74&amp;t=11</a>), this
corresponds to <math id="A7.p1.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="131.1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>131.1</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">131.1</annotation></semantics></math> simulated days per ton of CO<sub id="A7.p1.3.1" class="ltx_sub">2</sub>
vs. <math id="A7.p1.m14" class="ltx_Math" alttext="2.01" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>2.01</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2.01</annotation></semantics></math> for SCREAM.</p>
</div>
<figure id="A7.T5" class="ltx_table">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_table">Table S5: </span>Throughput and energy accounting assumptions for the SCREAM and
production STRATA comparison.
SCREAM SDPD from <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citet"><a href="#bib.bib5" title="" class="ltx_ref">Taylor et al. [5]</a></cite>;
Frontier system power (24,607 kW) from the TOP500 November 2025
list (<a href="https://top500.org/lists/top500/2025/11/" title="" class="ltx_ref ltx_url ltx_font_typewriter">https://top500.org/lists/top500/2025/11/</a>).
Both systems are assumed to draw their full rated power; in practice
utilization is lower, so the reported SD MWh<sup id="A7.T5.3" class="ltx_sup"><span id="A7.T5.3.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">-1</span></sup> values are
conservative lower bounds.</figcaption>
<table id="A7.T5.4" class="ltx_tabular ltx_centering ltx_guessed_headers ltx_align_middle">
<thead class="ltx_thead">
<tr id="A7.T5.4.1" class="ltx_tr">
<th id="A7.T5.4.1.1" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_th ltx_th_column ltx_th_row ltx_border_tt"><span id="A7.T5.4.1.1.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">System</span></th>
<th id="A7.T5.4.1.2" class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_th ltx_th_column ltx_border_tt"><span id="A7.T5.4.1.2.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Hardware</span></th>
<th id="A7.T5.4.1.3" class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_th ltx_th_column ltx_border_tt"><span id="A7.T5.4.1.3.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Power (kW)</span></th>
<th id="A7.T5.4.1.4" class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_th ltx_th_column ltx_border_tt"><span id="A7.T5.4.1.4.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">SDPD</span></th>

<section id="A8" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix H </span>Rollout Metrics</h2>

<section id="A8.SS0.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Precipitation amount distribution.</h4>

<div id="A8.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A8.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We follow the amount-distribution diagnostic of <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citet"><a href="#bib.bib57" title="" class="ltx_ref">Pendergrass and Hartmann [57]</a></cite> as described by
<cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citet"><a href="#bib.bib58" title="" class="ltx_ref">Kooperman et al. [58]</a></cite>, adapted from daily accumulated
rainfall to instantaneous precipitation rates.
For a sample set <math id="A8.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S=\{(k,t)\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>S</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>k</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S=\{(k,t)\}</annotation></semantics></math> over grid cells <math id="A8.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>k</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k</annotation></semantics></math> and frames <math id="A8.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>t</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t</annotation></semantics></math>, let
<math id="A8.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="a_{k}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>a</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a_{k}</annotation></semantics></math> be cell area and <math id="A8.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r_{kt}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>r</mi><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r_{kt}</annotation></semantics></math> be precipitation rate in mm day<sup id="A8.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_sup"><span id="A8.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">-1</span></sup>.
For logarithmic rain-rate bin
<math id="A8.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="B_{i}=\{(k,t):R_{i}^{\ell}\leq r_{kt}&lt;R_{i}^{r}\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>B</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>k</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>t</mi><mo rspace="0.278em" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mrow><msubsup><mi>R</mi><mi>i</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></msubsup><mo>≤</mo><msub><mi>r</mi><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow></msub><mo>&lt;</mo><msubsup><mi>R</mi><mi>i</mi><mi>r</mi></msubsup></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">B_{i}=\{(k,t):R_{i}^{\ell}\leq r_{kt}&lt;R_{i}^{r}\}</annotation></semantics></math> with
<math id="A8.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Delta\ln R=\ln(R_{i}^{r}/R_{i}^{\ell})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mo lspace="0.167em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mi>ln</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><mi>R</mi></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>ln</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msubsup><mi>R</mi><mi>i</mi><mi>r</mi></msubsup><mo>/</mo><msubsup><mi>R</mi><mi>i</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></msubsup></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Delta\ln R=\ln(R_{i}^{r}/R_{i}^{\ell})</annotation></semantics></math>, we compute</p>
<table id="A8.E9" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A8.E9.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p_{i}=\frac{1}{N_{T}\,\Delta\ln R}\sum_{(k,t)\in B_{i}}a_{k}r_{kt},\qquad N_{T}=\sum_{(k,t)\in S}a_{k}." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>p</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mrow><msub><mi>N</mi><mi>T</mi></msub><mo lspace="0.170em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mo lspace="0.167em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mi>ln</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><mi>R</mi></mrow></mrow></mfrac><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><munder><mo movablelimits="false">∑</mo><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>k</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>∈</mo><msub><mi>B</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></mrow></munder><mrow><msub><mi>a</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>r</mi><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow></msub></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="2.167em">,</mo><mrow><msub><mi>N</mi><mi>T</mi></msub><mo rspace="0.111em">=</mo><mrow><munder><mo movablelimits="false">∑</mo><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>k</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>∈</mo><mi>S</mi></mrow></munder><msub><mi>a</mi><mi>k</mi></msub></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p_{i}=\frac{1}{N_{T}\,\Delta\ln R}\sum_{(k,t)\in B_{i}}a_{k}r_{kt},\qquad N_{T}=\sum_{(k,t)\in S}a_{k}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(9)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A8.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.2" class="ltx_p">Dry samples are included in <math id="A8.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N_{T}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>N</mi><mi>T</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N_{T}</annotation></semantics></math> but not assigned to any rainy bin.
Thus <math id="A8.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sum_{i}p_{i}\Delta\ln R" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mo>∑</mo><mi>i</mi></msub><mrow><msub><mi>p</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mo lspace="0.167em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mi>ln</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><mi>R</mi></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sum_{i}p_{i}\Delta\ln R</annotation></semantics></math> equals the area-weighted global-mean
precipitation rate contributed by the plotted rain-rate range.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A8.SS0.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Fractions Skill Score (FSS).</h4>

<div id="A8.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A8.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We follow standard practice to reward realistic spatial structure of organized rainfall systems without
penalizing misplacement of individual convective cells by using the Fractions Skill Score
<cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib45" title="" class="ltx_ref">45</a>]</cite>.
Let <math id="A8.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hat{r}(\mathbf{x},t)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>r</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝐱</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{r}(\mathbf{x},t)</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A8.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r(\mathbf{x},t)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝐱</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r(\mathbf{x},t)</annotation></semantics></math> denote the model and
SCREAM reference precipitation rates (mm day<sup id="A8.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_sup"><span id="A8.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">-1</span></sup>) at grid cell
<math id="A8.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{x}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>𝐱</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{x}</annotation></semantics></math> and lead time <math id="A8.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>t</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t</annotation></semantics></math>.
For a threshold <math id="A8.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>T</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">T</annotation></semantics></math> (mm day<sup id="A8.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.2" class="ltx_sup"><span id="A8.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.2.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">-1</span></sup>), we form binary exceedance
indicators</p>
<table id="A8.E10" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A8.E10.m1" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="I_{\hat{r}}(\mathbf{x})=\mathbf{1}[\hat{r}(\mathbf{x})&gt;T],\qquad I_{r}(\mathbf{x})=\mathbf{1}[r(\mathbf{x})&gt;T]." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>I</mi><mover accent="true"><mi>r</mi><mo>^</mo></mover></msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝐱</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>𝟏</mn><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mover accent="true"><mi>r</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝐱</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>&gt;</mo><mi>T</mi><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><mo rspace="2.167em">,</mo><msub><mi>I</mi><mi>r</mi></msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝐱</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>𝟏</mn><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mi>r</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝐱</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>&gt;</mo><mi>T</mi><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">I_{\hat{r}}(\mathbf{x})=\mathbf{1}[\hat{r}(\mathbf{x})&gt;T],\qquad I_{r}(\mathbf{x})=\mathbf{1}[r(\mathbf{x})&gt;T].</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(10)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A8.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.2" class="ltx_p">Each indicator field is then averaged over a square <math id="A8.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="n\times n" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mi>n</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">n\times n</annotation></semantics></math> window
of neighboring grid cells to obtain local exceedance fractions:</p>
<table id="A8.E11" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A8.E11.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="F_{\hat{r}}(\mathbf{x})=\frac{1}{n^{2}}\sum_{\mathbf{x}^{\prime}\in\mathcal{N}_{n}(\mathbf{x})}I_{\hat{r}}(\mathbf{x}^{\prime}),\qquad stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝐱</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><msup><mi>n</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mfrac><mo lspace="0em" lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝐱</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></munder><mrow><msub><mi>I</mi><mover accent="true"><mi>r</mi><mo>^</mo></mover></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>𝐱</mi><mo>′</mo></msup><mo <td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(11)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A8.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.3" class="ltx_p">where <math id="A8.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{N}_{n}(\mathbf{x})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒩</mi><mi>n</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝐱</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{N}_{n}(\mathbf{x})</annotation></semantics></math> is the <math id="A8.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="n\times n" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mi>n</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">n\times n</annotation></semantics></math> neighborhood
centered on <math id="A8.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{x}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>𝐱</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{x}</annotation></semantics></math>.
The FSS is</p>
<table id="A8.E12" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A8.E12.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{FSS}=1-\frac{\displaystyle\sum_{\mathbf{x}}(F_{\hat{r}}(\mathbf{x})-F_{r}(\mathbf{x}))^{2}}{\displaystyle\sum_{\mathbf{x}}(F_{\hat{r}}(\mathbf{x})^{2}+F_{r}(\mathbf{x})^{2})}," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>FSS</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mfrac><mrow><mstyle displaystyle="true"><munder><mo movablelimits="false">∑</mo><mi>𝐱</mi></munder></mstyle><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>F</mi><mover accent="true"><mi>r</mi><mo>^</mo></mover></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝐱</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><msub><mi>F</mi><mi>r</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝐱</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><mrow><mstyle displaystyle="true"><munder><mo movablelimits="false">∑</mo><mi>𝐱</mi></munder></mstyle><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>F</mi><mover accent="true"><mi>r</mi><mo>^</mo></mover></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝐱</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><msub><mi>F</mi><mi>r</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝐱</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mfrac></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{FSS}=1-\frac{\displaystyle\sum_{\mathbf{x}}(F_{\hat{r}}(\mathbf{x})-F_{r}(\mathbf{x}))^{2}}{\displaystyle\sum_{\mathbf{x}}(F_{\hat{r}}(\mathbf{x})^{2}+F_{r}(\mathbf{x})^{2})},</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(12)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A8.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.4" class="ltx_p">ranging from 0 (no overlap) to 1 (perfect agreement).
The pooling is applied independently per cubed-sphere face with reflect
padding (edge values mirrored outward) and does not cross face boundaries.
To obtain a single global score, numerator and denominator are accumulated
across all six faces before forming the ratio.
We report FSS against a persistence baseline (SCREAM truth held constant
at the initial time <math id="A8.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t_{0}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>t</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t_{0}</annotation></semantics></math>), with the same binarization, pooling, and
aggregation applied to both.</p>
</div>
<figure id="A8.F7" class="ltx_figure"><object type="image/svg+xml" data="2606.31248v1/init_sweep_fss_grid_n6_T120-T480-T1200_n2-n5-n10.svg" id="A8.F7.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_square" style="aspect-ratio:471/419;" width="471" height="419"></object>
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure">Figure S7: </span><span id="A8.F7.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">FSS sensitivity to precipitation threshold and neighborhood size.</span>
Each panel shows Fractions Skill Score (FSS) versus lead time for STRATA
(blue) and persistence (red), with shading indicating the spread across
initializations. Rows use fixed precipitation thresholds of 120, 480, and
1200 mm day<sup id="A8.F7.5" class="ltx_sup"><span id="A8.F7.5.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">-1</span></sup>, corresponding to increasingly intense rainfall.
Columns use pooling neighborhoods of <math id="A8.F7.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="2\times 2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2\times 2</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="A8.F7.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="5\times 5" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>5</mn><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">5\times 5</annotation></semantics></math>, and <math id="A8.F7.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="10\times 10" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>10</mn><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mn>10</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">10\times 10</annotation></semantics></math>
native grid cells (<math id="A8.F7.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{\approx}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>≈</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{\approx}</annotation></semantics></math>10, 24, and 49 km). The dashed line marks
FSS = 0.5, a common scale-dependent reference for useful neighborhood
agreement. As expected, FSS decreases faster for smaller neighborhoods and
higher precipitation thresholds.
</figcaption>
</figure>
</section>
</section>

<section id="A10" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix J </span>Information Entropy: Details
</h2>

<div id="A10.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A10.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Section <a href="#S4.SS2" title="4.2 Scaling transformers for high-entropy data ‣ 4 Experiments ‣ Scaling Storm-Resolving Atmospheric AI Simulation to the Entire Planet" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4.2</span></a> argued that km-scale data is higher entropy and therefore requires more compute for a given level of accuracy than coarser resolution modeling.</p>
</div>
<div id="A10.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A10.p2.1" class="ltx_p">To support this interpretation, we compute the differential entropy of spatial patches of size <math id="A10.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>p</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p</annotation></semantics></math> of <math id="A10.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="dx\in\mathbb{R}^{cp^{2}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mrow><mi>c</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>p</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">dx\in\mathbb{R}^{cp^{2}}</annotation></semantics></math> assuming a Gaussian distribution <math id="A10.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="dx\sim\mathcal{N}(0,\Sigma)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><mo>∼</mo><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒩</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">Σ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">dx\sim\mathcal{N}(0,\Sigma)</annotation></semantics></math>. The number of output dimensions is <math id="A10.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>d</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d</annotation></semantics></math>. To make this comparable across dataset with different units we unit normalize this so that <math id="A10.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Sigma_{ii}=1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Σ</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>i</mi></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Sigma_{ii}=1</annotation></semantics></math>. Given the large spatial resolution, we estimate this from a single time <math id="A10.p2.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>t</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t</annotation></semantics></math> for convenience. The entropy in bits/dim <math id="A10.p2.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="c=cp^{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>c</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>c</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>p</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">c=cp^{2}</annotation></semantics></math> is given by <math id="A10.p2.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H/d=\frac{\ln(2)}{2d}(d+d\ln(2\pi)+\ln|\Sigma|)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>H</mi><mo>/</mo><mi>d</mi></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>ln</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>d</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo>+</mo><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo lspace="0.167em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mi>ln</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>π</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><mi>ln</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">Σ</mi><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H/d=\frac{\ln(2)}{2d}(d+d\ln(2\pi)+\ln|\Sigma|)</annotation></semantics></math>. Table <a href="#A10.T6" title="Table S6 ‣ Appendix J Information Entropy: Details ‣ Scaling Storm-Resolving Atmospheric AI Simulation to the Entire Planet" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">S6</span></a> shows this quantity for several patch sizes. It shows that the SCREAM target carries significantly more information per dimension especially when more spatial context is included (larger <math id="A10.p2.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>p</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p</annotation></semantics></math>). For an 8x8 patch, the entropy of SCREAM is 6 bits/dim larger than ERA5 and substantially closer to white noise (2 bits/dim; the maximum entropy distribution)—than ERA5.
We suspect that this additional entropy increases the computational demand (harmful) but at the same time the information density is helpful for training models on a limited number of samples.</p>
</div>
<div id="A10.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A10.p3.1" class="ltx_p">Qualitatively, this can be visualized comparing the covariance structure of the state-vector difference <math id="A10.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="dx=x(t+\Delta t)-x(t)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>+</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">dx=x(t+\Delta t)-x(t)</annotation></semantics></math> for SCREAM and ERA5 in a single atmospheric column. Figure <a href="#A3.F4" title="Figure S4 ‣ Evaluation initializations. ‣ C.2 Training Data ‣ Appendix C Dataset details ‣ Scaling Storm-Resolving Atmospheric AI Simulation to the Entire Planet" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">S4</span></a> shows that ERA5 targets have much stronger correlation across vertical levels and variables.</p>
</div>
<figure id="A10.T6" class="ltx_table">
<div class="ltx_flex_figure ltx_flex_table">
<div class="ltx_flex_cell ltx_flex_size_1">
<table id="A10.T6.2" class="ltx_tabular ltx_centering ltx_figure_panel ltx_guessed_headers ltx_align_middle">
<thead class="ltx_thead">
<tr id="A10.T6.2.1" class="ltx_tr">
<th id="A10.T6.2.1.1" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_th ltx_th_column ltx_th_row ltx_border_tt">Dataset</th>
<th id="A10.T6.2.1.2" class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_th ltx_th_column ltx_border_tt">1x1</th>
<th id="A10.T6.2.1.3" class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_th ltx_th_column ltx_border_tt">2x2</th>
<th id="A10.T6.2.1.4" class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_th ltx_th_column ltx_border_tt">4x4</th>
<th id="A10.T6.2.1.5" class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_th ltx_th_column ltx_border_tt">8x8</th></tr>
</thead>
<tbody class="ltx_tbody">
<tr id="A10.T6.2.2" class="ltx_tr">
